brief: Lane hb: stages R0-R2 of hybrid continuous batching for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (NVFP4) on HIP (AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201, tatooine), mirroring rb2 on CUDA: G-B row-exact kernels for every decode kernel the 35B uses at M = 1..16, rows_exact registered on HIP for what passes, cap from G-B and VRAM, batched logits bitwise equal to solo (G-C), batched engine bitwise to LocalEngine, batching-off no-op, localeval speed at 1/4/16 streams.
hypothesis: The HIP 1-row decode kernels are row-independent in their arithmetic and only their dispatch is M-dependent (instantiations stop at M = 4 / 8, WMMA above), so row-exact _rows twins are cheap; batching dense projections and MoE tokens with GDN and attention per row should lift 4- and 16-stream aggregate decode well above the single-sequence 135 tok/s with every row bitwise the solo step.

summary: HIP now batches the hybrid 35B with every row bitwise the solo step: five rows_exact kernels (fp8, nvfp4, bf16, logits GEMV, MoE experts) pass G-B at M 1..16, G-C is 17550 identical (row, step) pairs for N 2..16, the batched engine equals LocalEngine, and batching off is byte-identical to main. localeval aggregate decode with --max-batch 16: 157.8 / 195.2 / 234.7 tok/s at 1 / 4 / 16 streams against 158.2 / 134.7 / 135.0 on main (x1.45 at 4, x1.74 at 16). The step is eager and the fp8/nvfp4 multi-row GEMVs are ALU-bound past 4 rows, so 16 streams stay far from the bandwidth bound.
lessons: A test that sets INTARSIA_BATCH_TEST_BACKEND outside the dev container runs the cpu path: dev.sh forwards only INTARSIA_HIP_* and INTARSIA_TP_* variables, so a first all-green run proved nothing. Set the variable inside the container.

Fusions without a fusion-table entry are taken away from the solo step when batching is on (the row-count probe in fused_ok): a single stream lost 11% until the HIP phase-1 folds got entries. Check the single-stream number with batching on, not only the aggregate.

The HIP v2 nvfp4 GEMV is 4x slower per row at M = 8 than at M = 4 (register footprint); grouping rows by 4 beat one M = 8 launch (head: 1.5 ms against 3.3 ms), and row-exactness makes the grouping free.
HIP's tensor-core MoE path starts at 16 tokens and is not row-exact against T = 1 (57 of 2048 elements differ): the rows entry must never take it, whatever INTARSIA_HIP_MOE_WMMA says.

Busy prefill chunk 1024 was also identical to the solo chunk on HIP on four long prompts; the default stays the solo chunk (bitwise by construction), so this is not evidence the stall can be shortened.
